flows.title: From the Mongols to Unit 3
steps: Mongol Empire splits into rival khanates
Black Death and revolts weaken Mongol power (1340s–1368)
Power vacuum across Asia
Turkic and other new states use gunpowder to fill it
Ottoman, Safavid, Mughal, Qing and Russian empires expand

flows.title: How a land empire works (the Unit 3 pattern)
steps: Gunpowder conquest
Many peoples and religions to rule
Loyal elites and professional armies
Legitimacy through religion, art and architecture
Revenue through taxes, tax farming and tribute
Overspending, weak heirs and revolts lead to decline

flows.title: Chaldiran and its effects
steps: 1501: Ismail I makes Shi'a Islam the Safavid state religion
1514: Ottoman guns beat Safavid cavalry at Chaldiran
Safavid expansion west stops
Abbas I rebuilds the army with muskets, artillery and ghulams
Sunni–Shi'a divide hardens between the two empires

flows.title: The Reformation and its wars
steps: 1517: Luther attacks indulgences
1521: Luther excommunicated; German princes back him
1540–1563: Jesuits approved; Council of Trent
1555: Peace of Augsburg (Catholic or Lutheran)
1618–1648: Thirty Years' War
1648: Peace of Westphalia (Calvinism added)

flows.title: Mughal rise and decline
steps: 1526: Babur wins at Panipat with cannons
Akbar: tolerance, ends jizya, Hindus in government
Shah Jahan builds the Taj Mahal
Aurangzeb: restores jizya, wars in the Deccan
Revolts and an empty treasury; Britain and France gain ground

flows.title: Sikhism: from teaching to self-defense
steps: Late 1400s: Guru Nanak founds Sikhism in Punjab
Akbar grants land to Sikhs
1604: Adi Granth installed at Amritsar
1606: Jahangir executes Guru Arjan
1699: Guru Gobind Singh founds the Khalsa

tables.title: The land empires at a glance
rows: SE Europe, Middle East, N. Africa
Shi'a Islam as state religion; Isfahan
Taxes used to push Shi'a Islam
Mandate of Heaven, Confucian exam, portraits
Tsar as Orthodox ruler; St. Petersburg

tables.title: Loyal elites compared
rows: No family ties; loyal only to the sultan
Educated, loyal; made the Manchus look Chinese
Paid by the shogun, not by feudal lords
Lower officials and merchants; promotion by service
Carried out the king's orders in the provinces

tables.title: Akbar vs. Aurangzeb
rows: Tolerance; Din-i Ilahi; land grants to Sikhs
Strict Sunni rule; opposed Hindu influences
Largest size, but empty treasury and decline

tables.title: Religion in the three Islamic empires (AMSCO)
rows: None; Ismail I forced Sunnis to convert
Qizilbash, then ghulams; no significant navy

tables.title: Legitimacy: religion, art, architecture
rows: Divine right (Europe); caliph claim (Ottoman); Mandate of Heaven (Qing); Mexica human sacrifice; Askia promotes Islam (Songhai); Sapa Inca as child of the sun
Qing imperial portraits; Ottoman miniature paintings; Mughal miniatures; European royal patronage
Taj Mahal; Versailles; Topkapi and Suleymaniye; Coricancha in Cusco; St. Petersburg; Isfahan

tables.title: Revenue systems
rows: Private collectors pay a fixed sum and keep any surplus
Local collectors take land taxes and keep a share
Conquered provinces send goods (Codex Mendoza: 38 provinces)
Land tax and labor combined into one silver payment (c. 1580)
1718: tax on each person replaces land tax

tables.title: Christianity splits
rows: Popes; Council of Trent; Ignatius of Loyola
Faith alone; Bible over Church hierarchy
King, not Pope, heads the church
Geneva, Huguenots in France, Scotland, Puritans
Southern Europe; missions to Asia and the Americas

cheat.title: The five-empire memory trick
items: Only Quietly Students Must Study = Ottoman, Qing, Safavid, Mughal, Songhai.
Plus Russia (AMSCO counts it as a gunpowder empire).

cheat.title: Contextualization sentence
items: "The collapse of the Mongol Empire left a power vacuum across Asia, and new empires used gunpowder weapons to fill it."

cheat.title: Three battles to know
items: 1514 Chaldiran: Ottoman guns beat Safavid cavalry (Sunni vs. Shi'a).
1526 Panipat: Babur's carts, cannons and matchlocks found the Mughal Empire.
1591 Tondibi: Moroccan muskets beat Songhai and take the gold routes.

cheat.title: SAQ checklist (TEA)
items: T: answer the question in its own words.
E: one specific name, place, term or date.
A: explain how it proves your point ("which led to," "because").
